records.name: IAM
records.definition: IAM is the identity service for users, roles, and policies in an AWS account.
useWhen: Choose IAM when an application needs a role whose permissions you write in a policy.
Choose IAM when you need to grant a person or workload access inside one account.
records.notFor: you want a company-wide sign-in directory across many accounts

lightning.claim: IAM users and roles are created separately in each Region.
lightning.correction: IAM is global. The same users, roles, and policies apply in every Region.

records.name: AWS IAM Identity Center
records.definition: IAM Identity Center is the workforce sign-in service for multiple AWS accounts.
useWhen: Choose IAM Identity Center when people need one sign-in to a set of accounts.
Choose IAM Identity Center when access should follow group membership rather than a new IAM user in every account.
records.notFor: a single application needs its own IAM role and no workforce directory

records.name: AWS Organizations
records.definition: AWS Organizations groups accounts and can apply a service control policy to them.
useWhen: Choose AWS Organizations when a company needs one bill and a policy boundary across accounts.

lightning.correction: A service control policy only filters permissions the account already has. It does not grant new ones.

records.name: AWS KMS
records.definition: AWS KMS creates and controls the keys other AWS services use for encryption.
useWhen: Choose AWS KMS when S3, EBS, or RDS should encrypt data with a key you can disable.
Choose AWS KMS when the application must call encrypt or decrypt without running its own key server.
Choose AWS KMS when the encryption key should stay in the Region with the data.
records.notFor: you need a dedicated hardware security module that you administer yourself

lightning.claim: A KMS key stored in one Region automatically decrypts data in every Region.
lightning.correction: A KMS key is Regional unless you are using a multi-Region key that you created for that purpose.

cost.reason: Compared with a dedicated HSM, a customer managed key is the lower tier. The us-east-1 anchor is the rate read from that pricing page.
cost.freeTier: 20,000 requests per month, calculated across all Regions where the service is available. Creation and storage of AWS managed and AWS owned keys are not charged.
cost.freeTierReason: Read from the pricing page.

anchor.amount: $1 per month, prorated hourly, for each KMS key you create. The Key storage section states this rate. The Region selector on the page was US East (N. Virginia) for key usage.

classes.purpose: A KMS key you create and manage. The key-storage price applies.

classes.name: AWS managed key
classes.purpose: A legacy key type. The concepts page says new AWS services stopped creating these in 2021 and use an AWS owned key by default.

classes.name: AWS owned key
classes.purpose: A KMS key an AWS service owns and manages for use in multiple accounts. It is not in your account.

classes.name: Symmetric encryption KMS key
classes.purpose: The key type integrated AWS services use to encrypt data they store. Those services do not encrypt with asymmetric KMS keys.

classes.name: Asymmetric KMS key
classes.purpose: A public and private key pair. The private key is created in AWS KMS and never leaves AWS KMS unencrypted.

records.name: AWS Secrets Manager
records.definition: Secrets Manager stores a secret and can rotate it for a supported database.

lightning.correction: S3 encryption uses a key, usually from KMS. Secrets Manager holds the credential, not the object.

lightning.correction: AWS WAF inspects web requests. A security group filters packets by protocol and port.
